chunks: Make whatever Allah has made obligatory upon you from your requests, and ask Him for the fulfillment of what He has asked of you. Let your ears hear the call of death before you are called by death. Indeed, the hearts of those abstemious in the world weep even if they laugh, and their grief intensifies even if they rejoice, and their self-hatred increases even if they are envied for what they are provided.

key_terms.اغْتُبِطُوا: They were envied / They were admired for their provision
key_terms.الزَّاهِدِينَ: Ascetics / Those who abstain from worldly attachment

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual characteristic of the ascetics (zahidun) in this world according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi frames this passage within the ethical discourse of *Zuhd* (asceticism), urging believers to align their supplications with the weight of divine obligations and to internalize the reality of death (*dhikr al-mawt*) as a spiritual anchor. It characterizes the true ascetic not by external renunciation, but by an inner state of *khawf* (awe) and *huzn* (melancholy) that persists even amidst worldly joy, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the heart's vigilance (*muraqaba*) over mere ritual performance.
